name: UnitTypeMetadataRecord
description: Recovered 88-byte per-unit-type metadata record in the data segment. The decompiler split this record into overlapping globals (`g_UnitTypeMetadataRecords`, `g_UnitSpriteFolders`, `g_UnitTypeFlags`, and the byte_512570+ tables), but the code consistently indexes it as a single family.

fields.name: localized_name_ptrs
fields.notes: Pointer to the localized name array used by battle logs and building/unit info screens. The decompiler emitted this header as `char *(*...)[102]`, but asm/xref evidence shows at least 35 type records and one duplicated commander localized-name triplet.

fields.name: sprite_folder_name
fields.notes: Folder stem used to build paths such as `units_go\peon?.s32` and the other unit sprite-sheet filenames.

fields.name: move_pixel_speed
fields.notes: Per-frame marching displacement used by the world and battle movement animators.

fields.name: move_tick_delay
fields.notes: Delay between successive movement animation updates.

fields.name: animation_frame_interval
fields.notes: Shared per-type animation tick interval used by world idle animation, battle idle animation, and the melee/ranged attack loops.

fields.name: animation_flags
fields.notes: Recovered animation-behavior bits. Bit0 enables looping idle animation updates on the world map and in battle.

fields.name: visual_class_index
fields.notes: Per-type visual/footprint class. Rendering subtracts it from sprite Y origin, redraw helpers use non-zero values to invalidate neighboring tiles, and `Unit_GetClassIndex` exposes the same table as a reusable class lookup.

fields.name: melee_attack_frame_count
fields.notes: Frame count for the `_a.s32` melee attack sheet.

fields.name: ranged_attack_frame_count
fields.notes: Frame count for the `_s.s32` ranged attack sheet.

fields.name: type_flags
fields.notes: Recovered flag word. Bit0 marks flying/airborne units; another bit still controls the 6-vs-10 initialization path at slot +11.

fields.name: road_move_cost
fields.notes: Road/track movement cost copied into merged stack movement profiles.

fields.name: terrain_move_costs[8]
fields.notes: Per-terrain movement-cost profile consumed through `g_TerrainMoveTableOffsets` by `Map_GetUnitTileMoveCostOrZero` and stack-level movement merging.

fields.name: melee_attack_sound_frame
fields.notes: Frame index inside the melee attack loop that triggers the melee attack sound.

fields.name: ranged_attack_sound_frame
fields.notes: Frame index inside the shot-animation loop that triggers the ranged attack sound.

fields.name: move_sound_stem
fields.notes: Per-type movement sound stem used to build `sfx\ruchy\<stem>...` paths in both world and battle movement audio.

fields.name: move_sound_variant_count
fields.notes: Number of alternating movement-sound variants for footstep-style movers.

fields.name: move_sound_base_volume
fields.notes: Default playback volume passed into `CSS_PlaySound` for movement audio.

evidence: The code indexes `g_UnitTypeMetadataRecords` by `22 * unitType`, i.e. 88 bytes per type, then reads both pointer fields and late-byte movement fields from the same base address.

The decompiler's `char *(*...)[102]` type on the base pointer is misleading if read literally as the roster size: asm xrefs expose at least 35 records, while the final commander pair reuses one localized-name pointer triplet.
Battle/UI helpers dereference field 0 as a localized name pointer array, while sprite loaders read field 4 as the folder stem used in `units_go`, `units_i`, and `units_at` asset paths.

World idle-animation helpers advance on bytes `+10` and `+11`, world/battle rendering use byte `+15` as the sprite Y-anchor offset, battle melee/ranged loops consume bytes `+16`, `+17`, `+79`, and `+80`, and movement-audio helpers read fields `+81`, `+85`, and `+86` from the same record family.

Movement helpers copy bytes `+29..+37` into a merged stack profile, while airborne flag checks read the overlapping flag dword at offset `+18`, proving these animation, movement, and audio bytes all coexist inside one 88-byte metadata record.

name: UnitMoveSpriteCacheEntry
base_symbol: g_UnitMoveSpriteCacheTypeIds / g_UnitMoveSpriteCacheOwnerIndices / g_UnitMoveSpriteCacheFacingDirections / g_UnitMoveSpriteCacheFrameIndices / g_UnitMoveSpriteCacheHandles / g_UnitMoveSpriteCacheLastUsedTicks
description: Recovered 15-byte LRU cache entry used by world-map and battle rendering to avoid reloading `units_go\...` movement sprite sheets.

fields.name: unit_type_id
fields.notes: Low 16 bits hold the cached unit type id; `-1` marks a free entry.

fields.name: owner_index
fields.notes: Player/color variant index that becomes the trailing digit in the `units_go\...<owner>.s32` filename.

fields.name: facing_direction
fields.notes: Facing bucket used when converting `(frame_index + 8 * facing_direction)` into a sprite index.

fields.name: frame_index
fields.notes: Low-three-bit animation frame within the movement sheet.

fields.name: sprite_handle
fields.notes: Loaded sprite-set handle returned to the renderer on cache hits.

fields.name: last_used_tick
fields.notes: Timestamp refreshed on hits and consulted by the LRU eviction pass on misses.

evidence: `UnitSpriteCache_Reset`, `UnitSpriteCache_Clear`, and `UnitSpriteCache_CountEntries` scan 1500 bytes in steps of 15, proving a fixed-size 100-entry cache family.
`UnitSpriteCache_LoadMoveSheet` stores the type id, owner index, facing, frame, handle, and timestamp at offsets `0`, `4`, `5`, `6`, `7`, and `11`, respectively.
`UnitSpriteCache_GetOrLoadMoveSheet` matches exactly those same fields before refreshing `last_used_tick` and returning the cached `sprite_handle`.

name: UnitStackRecord
description: Per-army stack record inside gameData holding tile coordinates, ownership, slots, and the queued world-map path buffer.

fields.name: tile_row
fields.notes: Row on the 200-column world grid used to stamp tile occupancy and fog-of-war.

fields.name: tile_column
fields.notes: Column on the world grid; combined with row to index TILE_INDEX.

fields.name: owner_player_index
fields.notes: Player id copied from PLAYER_DATA and reused by fog-of-war and turn-sensitive ownership checks via g_CurrentPlayerIndex.

fields.name: facing_direction
fields.notes: 0-7 direction used by sprite/orientation logic during path highlighting.

fields.name: unit_slots[10]
fields.notes: Ten embedded 31-byte slot records storing per-unit runtime state for the stack.

fields.name: queued_path
fields.notes: 404-byte queued path buffer copied in/out by qmemcpy during path planning and partially consumed by `UnitStack_ExecuteQueuedPath`.

fields.name: is_hidden_on_world_map
fields.notes: Non-zero while the stack is hidden. The hide action sets it, movement/splitting/merging clear it, and `UnitStack_RevealAndEngageHiddenEnemies` clears the same flag on revealed enemy stacks.

evidence: Unit_Create uses 147174 + 725 * index to address stacks, writing row/column/facing before stamping TILE_INDEX.
UnitSlot_InitFromType writes the slot fields (type id, owner, action points, health, fatigue, morale, and control bits) at offsets relative to stackPtr + 6.
UnitStack_UpdateVision and UnitStack_HasReadyUnits read these slots and field offsets to drive fog-of-war and readiness states.

Path planners copy exactly `0x194` bytes into offset `+316`, while `QueuedPath_StartsAtTile`, `QueuedPath_StartsInBuildingFootprint`, and `UnitStack_ExecuteQueuedPath` treat that region as a persistent queued-path buffer.

The hide-action helper refuses stacks whose byte `+720` is already set, then sets it after spending the turn; merge/split helpers clear the same byte, and `UnitStack_RevealAndEngageHiddenEnemies` clears it on exposed enemy stacks.

name: QueuedPathBuffer
description: 404-byte queued path buffer embedded inside each `UnitStackRecord` and returned by the world-map path planners.

fields.name: waypoint_count
fields.notes: Number of live waypoints currently stored in the queue. Zero means no queued path.

fields.name: waypoints[100]
fields.notes: Packed row/column/cumulative-cost waypoints. `UnitStack_ExecuteQueuedPath` consumes them from the tail and rewrites remaining cumulative costs after partial movement.

evidence: All world-map path generators allocate or copy exactly `404` bytes, matching one leading int plus 100 packed 4-byte nodes.
`QueuedPath_StartsAtTile` and `QueuedPath_StartsInBuildingFootprint` read `a1[1]`, proving the first live node begins immediately after the count word.
`UnitStack_ExecuteQueuedPath` repeatedly decrements the count, reads the tail node, and subtracts the already-spent cost from the high word of each remaining node.

name: PathWaypoint
description: Packed waypoint entry stored inside `QueuedPathBuffer`.

fields.name: tile_row
fields.notes: Low byte of the packed dword; compared directly against map rows by the queued-path guard helpers.

fields.name: tile_column
fields.notes: Second byte of the packed dword; compared directly against map columns by the queued-path guard helpers.

fields.name: cumulative_cost
fields.notes: High word storing the cumulative action-point cost to reach this waypoint from the stack's current origin.

evidence: `QueuedPath_StartsAtTile` compares the low two bytes of `waypoints[0]` against row and column parameters.
`UnitStack_ExecuteQueuedPath` checks the high word against `UnitStack_GetMinCurrentActionPoints` before consuming movement and later subtracts the already-spent cost from that same high word.
Building and temple approach generators trim the tail by comparing only the low two bytes of packed nodes against building-footprint coordinates, leaving the high word untouched until execution time.

name: UnitSlotRecord
description: Recovered 31-byte per-unit runtime slot embedded inside each UnitStackRecord.

fields.name: unit_type_id
fields.notes: -1 marks an empty slot; otherwise indexes the 88-byte unit-type metadata family.

fields.name: owner_player_index
fields.notes: Copied from the stack owner when the slot is initialized.

fields.name: current_action_points
fields.notes: Seeded from `g_UnitTypeBaseActionPoints` and recomputed from fatigue by `UnitSlot_CalcActionPointsFromFatigue` each new turn.

fields.name: current_health_percent
fields.notes: Starts at 100, scales the effective melee/ranged/damage helpers, drops to zero on death, and is also the slot-quality threshold used by the weak-unit detach/regroup helpers (`<= 10` for weak, `>= 8` for stronger regrouped entries).

fields.name: fatigue
fields.notes: 0-100 exhaustion counter. Thresholds at 80/90/100 reduce action points, and severe fatigue lowers morale each new turn.

fields.name: morale
fields.notes: Bounded 0-20 combat bonus and obedience score. Light-unit records seed this to 6, other units to 10.

fields.name: stance_bits
fields.notes: Low two bits feed melee/ranged/siege attack helpers directly; upper bits also drive garrison stance/formation cycling.

fields.name: state_flags
fields.notes: Bit 0x2 suppresses fatigue recovery for spent turns, bit 0x4 marks low-morale refusal, and bit 0x8 is the plague marker consumed by plague attrition and building/plague transfer logic.

fields.name: aux_runtime_state
fields.notes: Cleared on init and reused by battle/movement helper families; exact subfields remain unresolved.

fields.name: state_bits_2
fields.notes: Low bit is cleared on init and bit 0 influences ranged attack scaling in `UnitStats_CalcEffectiveRangedAttack`.

evidence: UnitSlot_InitFromType writes a stable 31-byte layout with type id, owner, current action points, health, fatigue, morale, and several control-bit clusters.
`UnitSlot_CalcActionPointsFromFatigue`, `Unit_NewTurn`, `Unit_CheckLowMorale`, and the attack helpers all reuse the same byte offsets, confirming the runtime-slot field boundaries.
The UI unit-info pane draws a damage bar from slot +9, morale badges from slot +11, and fatigue icons from slot +10, independently corroborating the field meanings.

`UnitStack_DetachWeakUnitsToAdjacentTile`, `UnitStack_DetachUnitTypeToAdjacentTile`, and the two regroup-by-health helpers all classify slots directly from byte `+9`, adding a second non-combat signal that this byte is the runtime health/strength percentage.

name: MapTileRecord
description: Per-tile terrain and overlay record inside gameData used by movement, bridge placement, and terrain-edge rendering.

fields.name: terrain_tile_id
fields.notes: Primary terrain id; movement helpers index `g_TerrainMoveProfileOffsets` with this word to select the terrain-specific byte_512586 move-cost column.

fields.name: overlay_tile_id
fields.notes: Secondary visual or edge overlay inspected by draw helpers when stitching neighboring coast and terrain-edge sprites.

fields.name: road_or_bridge_tile_id
fields.notes: Non-0xFFFF marks a road, bridge, or track overlay; movement switches to byte_512585 road costs when this word is present, and bridge code temporarily writes ids such as 872 here.

evidence: Map_GetUnitTileMoveCostOrZero and UnitStack_GetTileMoveCostOrZero read word 0 through `g_TerrainMoveProfileOffsets` and test word 2 for the road-cost fast path.

Bridge movement code at clash95.c:27193-27278 writes and later restores the word at offset +4 on the crossed tile and its neighbors, proving this field belongs to the tile record rather than a transient path buffer.
Main-map rendering reads the first two words of adjacent 14-byte entries to choose seam and edge sprites.

name: TileTrapOwnerMaskLayer
description: One-byte per tile owner mask for planted traps and revealed trap knowledge.

fields.name: owner_mask
fields.notes: Bit N marks player N as the trap owner or as having revealed the trap on that tile; the byte is cleared once the trap triggers.

evidence: Trap_New writes 1 << owner into gameData + 576374 + 100 * row + column when a trap is planted.
Trap_GetTileOwnerMask returns either the raw byte or a single-player bit test, and render code draws the trap marker only when the current player's bit is present.
Trap_ClearTileOwnerMask zeroes the byte, and Trap_TriggerAtStackTile clears the same location after damaging the moving stack.

name: PlayerRuntimeState
description: Per-player runtime state block embedded in gameData. Campaign, skirmish, and mission loaders reset this block before seeding player names, minimap/camera UI state, controller settings, religion/visibility state, queen state, and the deferred prisoner-placement queue.

fields.name: is_active
fields.notes: Set to 1 when a scenario loader enables this player slot; zeroed by `PlayerRuntimeState_ResetDefaults` for unused slots.

fields.name: display_name
fields.notes: Localized/player-entered ruler name copied in both campaign loaders and the multiplayer setup menu.

fields.name: camera_left
fields.notes: Saved strategic-map camera X position restored when this player becomes the viewed player.

fields.name: camera_top
fields.notes: Saved strategic-map camera Y position paired with `camera_left`.

fields.name: minimap_visible_flag
fields.notes: Per-player minimap visibility latch. The minimap show/hide/toggle actions update it, and minimap blits, hit-tests, and viewport dragging all early-out when it is clear.

fields.name: controller_mode
fields.notes: Multiplayer setup writes values 0, 1, or 2 here before `Scenario_LoadMultiplayerMapAndSeedPlayers`; many gameplay paths treat nonzero as locally controlled/human-visible.

fields.name: religion_flag
fields.notes: Boolean religious alignment flag. Religious-site entry checks and castle upgrade labels branch on this dword to choose the shrine-vs-cult and Christian-vs-pagan behavior.

fields.name: tech_level
fields.notes: Player-wide technology tier. New castles inherit its low three bits into `BuildingRecord.tech_level_bits`, technology progression raises it via the global upgrade check, and the tech-level notification helper compares it against `last_reported_tech_level`.

fields.name: last_reported_tech_level
fields.notes: Last technology tier already acknowledged by the player-facing notification path; `Player_ShowTechLevelAdvanceNotification` displays the message only when this differs from `tech_level`, then synchronizes it.

fields.name: battle_action_taken_flag
fields.notes: Set when the player performs a battle action such as movement, melee attack, or wall attack; the tactical turn loop resets it each round and uses it to decide whether to increment the inactivity counter.

fields.name: consecutive_idle_battle_turns
fields.notes: Counts consecutive tactical turns with no battle action taken. The battle loop increments it when `battle_action_taken_flag` stays clear and triggers `GodAnger` once it reaches two rounds.

fields.name: revealed_tiles_bitset[1300]
fields.notes: 13 bytes per map row storing the player's discovered/visible world tiles. `Map_IsTileVisibleToPlayer`, reveal stamping, and fog-of-war overlay classification all address this bitset directly.

fields.name: prisoner_transfer_queue[10]
fields.notes: Ten 6-byte entries cleared by `PlayerRuntimeState_ResetDefaults` and filled by `Prisoner_QueueCapturedUnit` before castles absorb new prisoners.

fields.name: queen_relationship_state
fields.notes: Broad queen state byte covering marriage status, relationship state, departure, and childbirth branches.

fields.name: queen_portrait_index
fields.notes: Portrait/sprite variant index chosen during the marriage-proposal path and reused by the proposal, whim, message, and relationship panels.

fields.name: queen_next_relationship_check_turn
fields.notes: Absolute turn threshold checked before the queen reviews this player's kingdom again.

evidence: `PlayerRuntimeState_ResetDefaults` clears a 1423-byte region, restores the default `doc` name at offset `+4`, and initializes the first byte of each embedded 6-byte prisoner-queue entry to `-1`.

Campaign and skirmish setup code copies five 1423-byte records into `gameData + 140024`, then `Scenario_LoadMultiplayerMapAndSeedPlayers` reads enabled flags, controller settings, and player names from that region while seeding the loaded map.

`MiniMap_ToggleVisibility`, `MiniMap_ShowAllLayers`, `MiniMap_ShowUnitsOnly`, `MiniMap_ShowBuildingsOnly`, and `MiniMap_Hide` all read or write the dword at offset `+23`, while `MiniMap_BlitDirtyRectAndDrawViewportBox`, `MiniMap_IsCursorInside`, and `MiniMap_UpdateViewportFromCursor` all early-out on the same field for the viewed player.

Religious-site entry rules and castle-construction labels read the dword at offset `+39` to choose the shrine-vs-cult / Christian-vs-pagan branch, so the field is a stable per-player religion/alignment flag.

Castle creation, castle capture, and the player tech-notification path converge on offsets `+47` and `+48`: new strongholds inherit the player's low-three-bit tech tier from `+47`, while `Player_ShowTechLevelAdvanceNotification` compares `+47` against `+48` before showing the advancement message and then copies the current tier into the reported slot.

Battle movement, melee attack, and wall-attack helpers all set the dword at offset `+49`, and the tactical turn loop resets or increments the paired dword at `+53` before calling `GodAnger`, proving this pair tracks per-player battle activity versus consecutive idle rounds.

`Map_IsTileVisibleToPlayer`, the reveal-stamping helpers, and the fog overlay classifier all index `13 * row + ((column) >> 3)` into offset `+57`, which fills the full 1300-byte gap up to the prisoner queue and establishes this range as the per-player revealed-tile bitset.

`Game_AdvanceToNextPlayerTurn` and map-load helpers store and restore the per-player camera through offsets `+15` and `+19`, while the queen proposal/message/whim UI and `Queen_NewTurn` use the final bytes at `+1419..+1421` as stable per-player queen relationship, portrait, and review fields.

name: WorldViewState
description: Shared gameData region that stores world dimensions, the active scripted mission id, the current camera origin, and which player owns the active turn versus the current human view.

fields.name: map_width_tiles
fields.notes: Horizontal tile count derived at map load and used to clamp camera movement.

fields.name: map_height_tiles
fields.notes: Vertical tile count derived at map load and used to clamp camera movement.

fields.name: map_view_left
fields.notes: Current leftmost visible tile in the main-map camera.

fields.name: map_view_top
fields.notes: Current topmost visible tile in the main-map camera.

fields.name: active_mission_index
fields.notes: `-1` for free/skirmish maps; otherwise indexes the scripted mission dispatcher, mission-status text table, and mission-specific victory/failure checks.

fields.name: turn_owner_player_index
fields.notes: Player id whose strategic turn is currently active; save/load restores g_CurrentPlayerIndex from this slot.

fields.name: viewed_player_index
fields.notes: Player id whose saved camera position and visibility should drive the current UI view; usually the current human player.

evidence: Map load computes offsets 140000 and 140004 by scanning the 14-byte tile grid until it reaches sentinel 0xFFFF rows and columns.
`UI_ShowMissionStatusPanel`, the post-victory mission-advance path, and the mission jump table rooted at `Scenario_LoadMissionByIndex` all treat offset `140017` as the active mission id.
Render_RestoreLostSurfaces, keyboard scrolling, and recentering clamp offsets 140008 and 140012 against the width and height fields, proving they are the camera origin.

Game_AdvanceToNextPlayerTurn persists PLAYER_CAMERA_LEFT/TOP for g_CurrentPlayerIndex, writes TURN_OWNER_PLAYER_INDEX when the acting player changes, and restores MAP_VIEW_LEFT/TOP from PLAYER_CAMERA_LEFT/TOP(VIEWED_PLAYER_INDEX).

name: BuildingRecord
description: Per-building gameplay record inside gameData holding tile ownership, garrison slots, add-ons, and local upgrade/resource state.

fields.name: tile_row
fields.notes: Building anchor tile row used with TILE_INDEX and building footprint stamping.

fields.name: tile_column
fields.notes: Building anchor tile column used with TILE_INDEX and adjacency scans.

fields.name: owner_player_index
fields.notes: Player id copied into spawned unit stacks and used for ownership, vision, and income lookups.

fields.name: footprint_class
fields.notes: Controls which neighboring offsets are legal for exit/spawn scans and which add-on requirement table to use; exact enum values remain ambiguous.

fields.name: display_name
fields.notes: In-record building/castle name string shown by construction and notification UI; `Building_AssignUniqueGeneratedName` overwrites this buffer when seeding a newly completed stronghold with a unique generated default name.

fields.name: garrison_slots[12]
fields.notes: Stored unit entries copied into and out of temporary army stacks by Building_UnitsLeave and Building_UnitGetInto.

fields.name: garrison_order_bytes[12]
fields.notes: Per-slot packed task bytes: bits `0..2` are the train/order countdown, while bits `3..5` are the repair countdown.

fields.name: addon_type_ids[12]
fields.notes: `-1` marks an empty add-on slot; buy/remove/select helpers treat this as the installed building add-on list.

fields.name: selected_addon_slot_index
fields.notes: Tracks the currently selected production-licence slot for `Building_SetUnitProduction` and `Building_StopUnitProduction`.

fields.name: castle_addon_flags
fields.notes: Castle add-on presence bits. Recovered mapping: bit `0x01` hospital, `0x02` barracks, `0x04` workshop, `0x08` school, `0x10` smiths; `Rules_AssertCastleFact` prints the same bit mapping as `szpital`, `koszary`, `warsztat`, `szkola`, and `kuznia`.

fields.name: construction_lock_flags
fields.notes: Bit 0 locks further castle add-on / wall-start actions while a staged construction or upgrade is already in progress; add-on builders set it, completion paths clear it, and `Castle_UpdateGateToggles` reads it to disable the management-screen controls.

fields.name: wall_strength
fields.notes: Returned by the `SilaMurow` rules host wrapper and incremented by staged wall-upgrade completion.

fields.name: upgrade_timer_turns
fields.notes: Per-turn countdown that gates completion of the staged upgrade tracked at `+421`.

fields.name: peasant_count
fields.notes: Returned by the `IloscChlopow` rules host wrapper and updated by `Building_UpdatePopulationGrowth`; the high nibble stores unrelated packed state bits.

fields.name: satisfaction
fields.notes: Returned by the `Zadowolenie` rules host wrapper and clamped between `0` and `100` during population-growth updates.

fields.name: plague_state
fields.notes: Low three bits store the active plague countdown/state. Building plague blocks gold collection, decays each turn in `Building_UpdatePlagueState`, and is seeded when a plagued stack enters a clean building.

fields.name: tax_rate
fields.notes: Returned by the `Podatek` rules host getter, adjusted by `ZmienPodatek`, multiplied into `Building_CollectGoldIncome`, and converted into a burden tier by `Building_GetTaxBurdenTier`; the upper two bits still carry unrelated packed state.

fields.name: stored_money
fields.notes: Returned by the `Pieniadze` rules host wrapper, spent by transfer and add-on purchase helpers, and replenished by `Building_CollectGoldIncome`.

fields.name: tech_level_bits
fields.notes: Low three bits are returned by the `PoziomTech` rules host wrapper and cap wall upgrades plus castle add-on availability.

fields.name: prisoner_slots[3]
fields.notes: Castle-only prisoner cells updated by `Prisoner_SetInCastles`, `Prisoner_NewTurn`, and the execution/torture/ransom helpers.

fields.name: castle_fact_id
fields.notes: Rules-engine handle returned by `Rules_AssertCastleFact`; `Rules_RetractCastleFact` clears it, `Building_OnGarrisonChange` updates its `moc` attribute, and `Unit_CaptureBuilding` updates its `gracz` owner attribute during capture.

evidence: Building_Transfer, Building_UnitsLeave, and Building_UnitGetInto all index `gameData + 509674 + 467 * buildingIndex`, proving a stable per-building stride and header.
The garrison move helpers copy 31-byte unit entries between `+18` and temporary stack records, showing that `+18` begins a 12-slot building garrison array.

The rules-host wrappers `Podatek`, `Pieniadze`, `SilaMurow`, `SilaZamku`, `PoziomTech`, `Zadowolenie`, and `IloscChlopow` dispatch directly to getters over offsets `+436`, `+438`, `+421`, `Building_GetTotalValue`, `+444`, `+434`, and `+430`, respectively.

Building buy/remove/select helpers at clash95.c:53980-54120 operate on `+402`, `+414`, and `+416`, while upgrade and income helpers use `+421`, `+429`, `+438`, and `+444`, exposing a second stable cluster for add-ons and local economy state.

`Building_AssignUniqueGeneratedName` copies randomized localized stronghold names into `building + 5`, and `Building_ShowConstructionProgressDialog` plus multiple event-notification paths print the same in-record buffer as the building display name.
The castle add-on builders and `Rules_AssertCastleFact` converge on the exact bit mapping at `+416`: `0x01` hospital, `0x02` barracks, `0x04` workshop, `0x08` school, `0x10` smiths.

Every castle add-on builder first checks bit 0 at `+420`, sets it when construction begins, and the completion/toggle paths clear or consult the same bit before enabling new castle build actions, proving it is the staged-construction lock byte.

`Building_GetTaxRateByIndex`, the `ZmienPodatek` host stub, `Building_CollectGoldIncome`, and `Building_GetTaxBurdenTier` all read or write the low six bits at `+436`, proving that byte carries the building's raw tax rate rather than a derived burden tier.

`Building_UpdatePlagueState`, `Building_CollectGoldIncome`, the plague-notification UI, and the stack-to-building infection transfer logic all read or write the low three bits at `+435`, proving that byte is the building plague state/countdown.

Prisoner_SetInCastles, BuildingPrisoner_SetAction, Prisoner_NewTurn, and Prisoner_Pay all operate on the 6-byte cells starting at `+445`, proving that the building record also embeds a fixed three-slot prison subarray.

`Rules_AssertCastleFact` stores its returned fact id at `+463`, `Rules_RetractCastleFact` retracts and clears the same dword, and `Building_OnGarrisonChange` plus `Unit_CaptureBuilding` use it to update the asserted castle fact's `moc` and `gracz` attributes.

name: PortRuntimeState
description: Six-dword world-session region inside gameData tracking the unique port's location and reinforcement schedule.

fields.name: port_tile_row
fields.notes: `-1` marks no port on the loaded map; otherwise this is the top-left row of the 2x2 port footprint.

fields.name: port_tile_column
fields.notes: Top-left column of the active port footprint.

fields.name: next_supply_turn
fields.notes: Absolute game-turn number when the next supply ship should arrive.

fields.name: supply_ready_flag
fields.notes: Non-zero while reinforcements are waiting to be claimed from the port.

fields.name: pending_supply_unit_count
fields.notes: Number of units to seed into the spawned reinforcement stack when the player collects the supply shipment.

fields.name: shoreline_variant_flag
fields.notes: Controls which shoreline-piece variant `Port_BuildShorePieces` renders for the current supply state.

evidence: `Port_FindAndInit` seeds all six dwords together after scanning the map for the unique port tile and then immediately calls `Port_BuildShorePieces` and `Rules_LogPortLocation`.
`Port_NewTurn`, `Port_BuildShorePieces`, and `Port_GetSupply` all read and mutate the same contiguous six-dword block to manage shipment timing, shoreline visuals, and spawned reinforcement contents.
The top-of-file offset macros in `clash95.c` and the matching xrefs in `clash95.asm` agree on the exact offsets `586374..586394` inside `gameData`.

name: PortSpawnOffset
description: One entry in the 12-cell shoreline spawn ring that `Port_GetSupply` probes around the 2x2 port footprint before creating the reinforcement stack.

fields.name: row_delta
fields.notes: Row offset from `PortRuntimeState.port_tile_row` to one candidate reinforcement spawn tile.

fields.name: column_delta
fields.notes: Column offset from `PortRuntimeState.port_tile_column` to the same candidate reinforcement spawn tile.

evidence: `Port_GetSupply` advances the two decompiled symbols in lockstep as 12 row/column pairs while scanning for the first empty and traversable shoreline-adjacent spawn tile, then reuses the same pair when creating and facing the reinforcement stack.

fields.notes: Focused slot index used by the detail-panel renderer and detail-sprite reload path.

fields.name: selected_unit_sprite_set
fields.notes: Sprite-set handle for the currently focused garrison unit.

fields.name: selected_unit_animation_frame
fields.notes: Animation frame advanced modulo eight by the selected-unit animation tick.

fields.name: slot_sprite_sets[12]
fields.notes: Per-slot sprite-set handles used by the slot-grid renderer.

fields.name: unnamed_slot_animation_state[24]
fields.notes: Adjacent per-slot animation/timing state. It is clearly part of the same modal block, but this pass did not freeze more specific names.

fields.name: pending_exit_countdown
fields.notes: Countdown armed by `BuildingGarrisonDialog_BeginSelectedUnitsExit` and consumed by `BuildingGarrisonDialog_TickExitCountdown` before calling `Building_UnitsLeave`.

evidence: `BuildingGarrisonDialog_DrawSlotGrid`, `BuildingGarrisonDialog_DrawSelectedUnitPanel`, and the repair/training/exit callbacks all share the same globals for active building, selection state, and pending-exit countdown.

`BuildingGarrisonDialog_ReloadSelectedUnitDetailSprites` and `BuildingGarrisonDialog_AnimateSelectedUnit` prove that the selected-unit sprite handle and animation frame are stable shared modal state, not temporary locals.
Asm-backed subagent evidence tied the same address range to the dialog runner setup and teardown, confirming that these globals belong to one building-garrison dialog state region.

name: MergedTerrainMoveProfile
base_symbol: UnitTypeMetadataRecord + 29 / stack-local buffers built by UnitStack_BuildMergedTerrainMoveProfile
description: Nine-byte movement-cost slice shared between each unit-type metadata record and the temporary stack-local profile buffers used by world-map pathfinding.

fields.name: road_or_bridge_move_cost
fields.notes: Road/bridge movement cost returned directly when the tile record carries a road or bridge overlay.

fields.name: terrain_move_costs[8]
fields.notes: Per-terrain movement costs indexed through `g_TerrainMoveProfileOffsets[*terrain_tile_id]` when the tile has no road overlay.

evidence: `UnitStack_BuildMergedTerrainMoveProfile` iterates the occupied 31-byte squad slots, loads each member's metadata record, and merges bytes `+29..+37` into an 88-byte temporary buffer.
`UnitStack_GetTileMoveCostFromMergedProfileOrZero` consumes that temporary buffer without rebuilding it, reading byte `29` for road/bridge overlays and bytes `30..37` for terrain-specific costs.

The merge logic keeps the highest non-zero cost for each byte and collapses to zero when any member contributes zero, so a stack moves at the slowest traversable rate of its constituent unit types and becomes impassable where any member cannot enter.

name: UnitStackSelectionState
description: Shared modal state for the world-map stack split/selection panel. The same globals drive panel activation, which stack is bound to the panel, which of the 10 slots are marked, and which info sprite set is loaded for the current dialog strip.

fields.name: active_stack_index
fields.notes: Actual symbol `dword_514194`. `-1` when the split panel is inactive; otherwise holds the selected stack index bound to the panel.

fields.name: dialog_active
fields.notes: Actual symbol `dword_526994`. World-map redraw and modal-loop helpers treat this as the split-panel activity latch.

fields.name: selected_slot_mask[10]
fields.notes: Actual symbol `dword_526F78`. One dword per slot; non-zero means the unit is marked for transfer or subset movement.

fields.name: active_stack_ptr
fields.notes: Actual symbol `dword_526FA0`. Cached pointer to the 725-byte stack record currently rendered in the strip.

fields.name: info_sprite_set_handle
fields.notes: Actual symbol `dword_527C24`. Sprite set loaded from `info%d.s32` and reused by the split-panel renderer.

evidence: `UnitStackSelection_SyncForCurrentSelection` opens, closes, or refreshes the split panel based on `g_SelectedUnitIndex`, current squad size, and whether `active_stack_index` is already latched.

`UnitStackSelection_RedrawPanel`, `UnitStackSelection_HandleInput`, and `UnitStack_ShowSelectionDialog` all share the same selected-slot mask, active-stack pointer, and dialog-active latch when drawing the strip and moving only marked squad members.
Asm-backed subagent evidence also ties `dword_527C24` to the `info%d.s32` unit-info sprite family used exclusively by this panel cluster.

name: BattlePathingTables
description: Shared tactical-battle pathing scratch state. The code precomputes per-tile movement costs, keeps a per-unit-type airborne move-cost table, and toggles whether occupied tiles should be treated as blocked.

fields.name: tile_move_cost_grid
fields.notes: Actual symbol `byte_531890`. `UnitBattle_InitPathingTables` fills this scratch grid from the battle map, using zero for impassable wall tiles and `BattleRuntimeState.default_tile_move_cost` for traversable ground.

fields.name: air_move_cost_by_unit_type
fields.notes: Decompiler-split symbols `byte_531C8F` and `byte_531C90` are one overlapping table. `UnitBattle_InitPathingTables` seeds it from `g_UnitTypeFlags bit0`, and `UnitBattle_GetTileMoveCostOrZero` returns fixed tactical move cost `5` for flagged airborne types.

fields.name: ignore_occupancy_flag
fields.notes: Actual symbol `dword_531CB8`. When clear, occupied tactical tiles return move cost zero; some movement probes raise it temporarily to ignore blockers.

evidence: `UnitBattle_InitPathingTables` iterates the tactical map dimensions, writes the per-tile cost scratch grid, then seeds the per-type airborne table by copying `g_UnitTypeFlags bit0` into the overlapping `byte_531C8F/byte_531C90` slab.

`UnitBattle_GetTileMoveCostOrZero` first rejects occupied tiles unless `ignore_occupancy_flag` is set, then returns fixed cost `5` for airborne types and otherwise falls back to the precomputed per-tile grid.
Callers such as `UnitBattle_MoveTrack`, AI movement probes, and the near-move helpers all consult the same grid/table/flag family, proving one shared tactical pathing state region.
